tournament|2020 Tokyo]]|[[2020 United States men's Olympic basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''JaVale Lindy McGee''' ({{IPAc-en|dʒ|ə|ˈ|v|eɪ|l}} {{respell|jə|VAYL}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.xom|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=June 7, 2024}} born January 19, 1988) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Beijing Ducks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada Wolf Pack]] and was selected 18th overall by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. McGee is a three-time [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]], having won consecutive titles with the [[Golden State Warriors]] in 2017 and 2018 before winning a third title with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2020. The son of Olympic gold medalist [[Pamela McGee]], he won a gold medal with the [[2020 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2020 U.S. Olympic team]]. ==High school and college career== McGee was born in [[Flint, Michigan]], and attended two high schools in [[Michigan]], [[Detroit Country Day School]] and Providence Christian, before transferring to [[Hales Franciscan High School]] in [[Chicago]], [[Illinois]].{{Cite web |date=November 5, 2005 |title=Nevada lands Chicago high school standout McGee |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2214303 |access-date=2025-06-01 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} According to Hales Franciscan coach Gary London, McGee's natural position in college was ideally [[small forward]], and he could play both [[forward (basketball)|forward]] spots. McGee was the starting center for the [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|University of Nevada]]. After averaging 14.3 points and 7.3 rebounds and shooting 53% from the field and 33% from three-point range as a sophomore, McGee decided to hire an agent and declare for the 2008 NBA draft.{{cite web|url=http://www.seattlepi.com/cbasketball/357199_mcgee01.html|title='Big Secret' out at Nevada; McGee declares for draft|date=April 2008 }} ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards (2008–2012)=== McGee was selected 18th overall by the Wizards in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. On July 9, 2008, he signed a two-year, $2.4 million deal with the Wizards.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3480795|title=Nevada C McGee signs rookie deal with Wizards|date=July 9, 2008|publisher=ESPN}} [[File:34McGee2010.jpg|thumb|upright|left|McGee in 2010]] On January 9, 2010, the Wizards fined McGee $10,000 for participating in [[Gilbert Arenas]]' antics before a game against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] four days prior. Arenas was being investigated for a prior incident involving guns in the Wizards' locker room, but made light of the accusations by pointing his finger at his teammates, as if he were shooting them. His teammates were photographed smiling and laughing with him.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4810297|title=Wizards fine 4 players involved in Arenas' antics|date=January 9, 2010|publisher=ESPN}} On January 6, 2011, McGee was chosen to participate in the 2011 [[NBA Slam Dunk Contest]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2011/news/01/05/sprite-slam-dunk-participants/index.html|title=Griffin, Ibaka, Jennings and McGee set for Sprite Slam Dunk |publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=April 5, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110109145216/http://www.nba.com/2011/news/01/05/sprite-slam-dunk-participants/index.html|archive-date=January 9, 2011}} He was the first Wizard to ever participate in the contest. McGee finished in second place, losing to [[Blake Griffin]]. McGee was the first player to use three balls at one time in a dunk contest, which was later cited by the [[Guinness World Records]] as the most basketballs dunked in a single jump. The third ball was passed to him from teammate [[John Wall]]. On March 15, 2011, in a 98–79 loss against the [[Chicago Bulls]], McGee notched his first career triple-double, recording 11 points, 12 rebounds, and 12 blocks. McGee's career-high 12 blocks was the most since [[Keon Clark]] had 12 on March 23, 2001.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310315004|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170719124025/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310315004|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 19, 2017|title=Despite JaVale McGee's triple-double, Bulls best Wizards to gain control of first in East|date=March 15, 2011|access-date=March 18, 2011|publisher=ESPN}} However, McGee received some criticism for taking ill-advised shots in the fourth quarter to ensure he reached 10 points while his team was being blown out, and even received a technical foul for excessive celebration by pulling himself on the rim after a dunk for his final points. Television commentator [[Kevin McHale (basketball)|Kevin McHale]] called it a "bad triple-double".{{cite web|url=https://offthedribble.blogs.nytimes.com/2011/03/19/javale-mcgees-unusual-triple-double/|title=JaVale McGee's Unusual Triple-Double|first=Benjamin|last=Hoffman|date=March 19, 2011|access-date=August 7, 2017|website=Off the Dribble}} In response to the criticism, McGee said, "I got a triple-double. Who can say they got a triple-double? I'm not really worried about it."{{cite web|url=http://aol.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2011-03-18/javale-mcgee-responds-to-negative-reaction-to-triple-double|title=JaVale McGee responds to negative reaction to triple-double|access-date=March 18, 2011|work=Sporting News|archive-date=March 21, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110321210049/http://aol.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2011-03-18/javale-mcgee-responds-to-negative-reaction-to-triple-double|url-status=dead}} During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], NBPA leaders met with around 30 players on October 14 and stressed unity. McGee left the meeting early and told reporters there were some players "saying that they're ready to fold", but the majority was united.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7102787/nba-lockout-nbpa-leaders-meet-players-stress-unity|title=NBPA stresses unity in player meeting|date=October 16, 2011|publisher=ESPN|last2=McMenamin|first2=Dave|last1=Adande|first1=J.A.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111016153113/http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/7102787/nba-lockout-nbpa-leaders-meet-players-stress-unity|archive-date=October 16, 2011|url-status=live}} McGee later denied mentioning that players were ready to fold, but his comment was recorded by reporters.{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/javale-mcgee-denies-saying-nba-players-ready-to-fold-in-lockout/2011/10/14/gIQA22VNlL_blog.html|title=JaVale McGee denies saying NBA players 'ready to fold' in lockout|last=Lee|first=Michael|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=October 15, 2011|access-date=May 25, 2023}} [[Derek Fisher]] said that McGee had "no ability to make that statement" based on the limited time he spent at the meeting. McGee averaged over 10 points and eight rebounds in 2010–11 and 2011–12 with the Wizards.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mcgeeja01.html|title=JaVale McGee NBA & ABA Stats |publisher=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=April 5, 2014}} ===Denver Nuggets (2012–2015)=== On March 15, 2012, McGee was traded to the Nuggets along with [[Ronny Turiaf]] in a deal that sent [[Nenê]] to the Wizards.{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards-trade-javale-mcgee-and-nick-young/2012/03/15/gIQAhkhFFS_story.html|title=Wizards trade JaVale McGee, Nick Young and Ronny Turiaf for Nene, Brian Cook and a draft pick in three-team deal|date=March 15, 2012|access-date=May 25, 2023|last=Lee|first=Michael|newspaper=The Washington Post}} As a member of the Wizards, McGee started 40 of 41 games in which he appeared; with the Nuggets, he would start in five of 20 games in which he appeared. McGee's minutes would also be reduced, averaging 27.4 with Washington but 20.6 with [[2011–12 Denver Nuggets season|Denver]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mcgeeja01.html|work=Basketball-reference.com|title=JaVale McGee|access-date=May 17, 2012}} On March 21, in his Nuggets debut, McGee made the game-winning dunk off an [[Arron Afflalo]] missed free throw with five seconds left on the clock. At the end of the regular season, the Nuggets earned the West's sixth seed, and McGee appeared in the [[2012 NBA playoffs]], which was his first playoff appearance in his career. McGee's series-high was 21 points in Game 5 against first-round opponent [[2011–12 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/nuggets-avoid-elimination-hold-off-081055342--nba.html|title=Nuggets avoid elimination, hold off Lakers 102–99|agency=Associated Press|publisher=Yahoo! Sports|first=Greg|last=Beacham|date=May 9, 2012|access-date=May 17, 2012|archive-date=May 17, web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320512013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170708034525/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320512013|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 8, Nuggets on a four-year, $44 million contract.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-re-sign-free-agent-javale-mcgee|publisher=National Basketball Association|title=Nuggets re-sign free agent JaVale McGee|date=July 18, 2012|access-date=July 19, 2012}} McGee's 2013–14 season was ended on February 20, 2014, when he underwent surgery to repair a stress fracture in his left tibia in which he sustained on November 8, 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-center-javale-mcgee-undergoes-surgery|title=Denver Nuggets Center JaVale McGee Undergoes Surgery – Denver Nuggets|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] }} On October 29, 2014, McGee made his return for the Nuggets, recording two points and two rebounds in the season opening 89–79 victory Mavericks (2015–2016)=== On August 13, 2015, McGee signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite news|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-center-javale-mcgee/|title=Mavericks sign center Javale Mcgee|work=mavs.com|date=August 13, 2015|access-date=August 13, 2015}} He missed the team's first 13 games of the 2015–16 season due to a stress fracture in his left tibia. 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160710183252/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=19465|archive-date=July 10, 2016|url-status=dead}} ===Golden State Warriors (2016–2018)=== On September 16, 2016, McGee signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|title=Warriors Announce Roster & Schedule for 2016 Training Camp, Fueled by Gatorade|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/2016-training-camp-roster-20160916|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=September 16, 2016|access-date=September 16, 2016}}{{cite web|last=Letourneau|first=Connor|url=http://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/Warriors-sign-four-players-ahead-of-training-camp-9223391.php|title=Warriors sign four players ahead of training camp|work=San Francisco Chronicle|date=September 14, 2016|access-date=September 14, 2016}} On December 15, he scored a season-high 17 points in a 103–90 victory over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899830|title=Another efficient passing night leads Warriors past Knicks|publisher=ESPN|date=December 15, 2016|access-date=December 16, 2016}} On March 31, 2017, McGee had 13 points and a season-best five blocked shots in a 107–98 victory over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900531|title=Warriors use big fourth quarter to hold off Rockets 107–98|publisher=ESPN|date=March 31, 2017|access-date=April 1, 2017}} The Warriors went on to win the [[2017 NBA Finals]] after defeating the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in five games. McGee played in 77 of 82 regular season games, with a field goal percentage of .652, and 16 of 17 playoff games, with a percentage of .732, both the best in his career. The Warriors finished the playoffs with a 16–1 record, the best postseason winning percentage in NBA history.{{cite web |date=June 14, 2017 |title=Warriors (16–1) Record Best Postseason Winning Percentage in NBA History |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2715556-warriors-16-1-record-best-postseason-winning-percentage-in-nba-history |access-date=May 10, 2018 |website=Bleacher Report}} On August 1, 2017, McGee re-signed with the Warriors on a one-year contract.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/mcgee-re-signing-20170801|title=Warriors Re-Sign Center JaVale McGee|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=August 1, 2017|access-date=August 1, 2017}}{{cite web|last=Haynes|first=Chris|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/20176003|title=Sources: JaVale McGee re-signing with Warriors on 1-year deal|publisher=ESPN|date=July 27, 2017|access-date=July 28, 2017}} His playing time increased when he was inserted into the starting lineup after the all-star break.{{Cite web|url=https://www.goldenstateofmind.com/2018/7/9/17480012/nba-free-agency-2018-golden-state-warriors-season-review-zaza-pachulia-center|title=Warriors Season Review: The league has left Zaza Pachulia behind|last=Kitano|first=Hugo|date=July 9, 2018|website=Golden State Of Mind|language=en|access-date=December 30, 2019}} In June 2018, McGee won his second straight championship after the Warriors defeated the Cavaliers in a four-game sweep during the [[2018 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]]. McGee started the final three games of the series, and averaged 8.0 points in the four games.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mcgeeja01/gamelog/2018/|title=JaVale McGee 2017–18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=June 9, 2018}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2018–2020)=== On July 10, 2018, McGee signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180710-lakers-sign-javale-mcgee|title=Lakers Sign JaVale McGee|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 10, 2018|access-date=July 10, 2018}} He missed seven games in December due to a respiratory infection.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071217|title=Lakers rally in 4th quarter, defeat Kings 121–112|publisher=ESPN|date=December 30, 2018|access-date=December 31, 2018}} On March 22, 2019, McGee had career highs of 33 points and 20 rebounds to go along with six blocked shots during a 111–106 loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071759|title=Surging Nets eliminate Lakers from playoff picture, 111–106|publisher=ESPN|date=March 22, 2019|access-date=March 23, 2019}} During the 2019–20 season, McGee played in 68 games and averaged 6.6 points and 5.7 rebounds in 16.6 minutes per game. He won his third NBA championship as a member of the Lakers in 2020.{{Cite web|title=Cavaliers Acquire JaVale McGee from Los Angeles Lakers|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/mcgee-trade-201123|access-date=April 11, 2021|website=Cleveland Cavaliers|language=en}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2020–2021)=== On November 23, 2020, .542 || .356 || .514 || 4.8 || .3 || .5 || 1.8 || 8.7 {{S-end}} ==National team career== [[File:JaVale McGee USA basketball (cropped).JPG|thumb|upright|right|McGee during an exhibition match in 2009]] McGee received an invite to the [[United States men's national basketball team|U.S. national team]]'s mini-camp in the summer of 2009 and again in the summer of 2010.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/olybb/news/story?id=5393651|title=Wizards C McGee joins Team USA camp roster|date=July 20, 2010|publisher=ESPN}} He played with Team USA in a scrimmage at [[Radio City Music Hall]] during the 2010 World Basketball Festival,{{cite news | url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/wizardsinsider/2010/08/-javale-mcgee-has-uneven.html | url-status=dead | newspaper=The Washington Post | title=JaVale McGee has uneven outing in Team USA scrimmage | access-date=April 12, 2011 | archive-date=October 14, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121014201122/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/wizardsinsider/2010/08/-javale-mcgee-has-uneven.html }} but after an uneven performance, McGee did not play in the team's scrimmage against China at [[Madison Square Garden]] and was cut on August 15, 2010.{{cite web|url=http://www.rgj.com/article/20100816/SPORTS/8160311/1018/SPORTS|title=Sports | Reno Gazette-Journal |publisher=rgj.com|access-date=April 5, 2014}} McGee visited the [[Philippines]] twice during the [[2011 NBA lockout]], first in exhibition games with NBA stars against players from the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] and the [[Smart Gilas]] [[Philippines men's national basketball team|national team]], and then in a basketball clinic. Later that year, McGee expressed his interest in playing for the Philippine national team,{{cite web|url=http://deadspin.com/5854928/javale-mcgee-to-become-the-latest-non-filipino-on-the-philippines-national-basketball-team|title=JaVale McGee To Become The Latest Non-Filipino On The Philippines National Basketball Team (UPDATE)|first=Barry|last=Petchesky|date=October 31, 2011 }} and in 2012, a bill was filed for his Filipino citizenship to make him eligible to play for [[Smart Gilas]].{{cite web|url=http://www.gmanetwork.com/news/story/258288/sports/basketball/bill-seeking-to-grant-javale-mcgee-filipino-citizenship-filed|title=Bill seeking to grant JaVale McGee Filipino citizenship filed|date=May 15, 2012 }} In 2014, McGee was asked again by the [[Philippines men's national basketball team|Gilas Pilipinas]] to take part as a naturalized player for the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] in Spain.{{cite web|url=http://nba.nbcsports.com/2014/01/30/report-philippines-wants-to-naturalize-javale-mcgee-andray-blatche-before-world-championships/|title=Report: Philippines wants to naturalize JaVale McGee, Andray Blatche before World Championships|first=Kurt|last=Helin|date=January 30, 2014}} However, national teams were limited to one [[naturalized]] player apiece, and former Wizards teammate [[Andray Blatche]] made the World Cup team after he was granted citizenship.{{cite news |last=Dy |first=Richard |url=http://www.spin.ph/sports/pba/news/andray-blatche-now-eligible-to-play-for-gilas-as-president-aquino-signs-naturalization-papers-v02 |title=Andray Blatche now eligible to play for Gilas as President Aquino signs naturalization papers |date=June 11, 2014 |work=spin.ph |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141031135108/http://www.spin.ph/sports/pba/news/andray-blatche-now-eligible-to-play-for-gilas-as-president-aquino-signs-naturalization-papers-v02 |archive-date=October 31, 2014 |url-status=dead |access-date=February 6, 2015 }}{{cite news|title=Douthit for Blatche, Alapag for Castro |date=September 12, 2014 |newspaper=Philippine Daily Inquirer |url=http://sports.inquirer.net/164012/douthit-for-blatche-alapag-for-castro |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150207003327/http://sports.inquirer.net/164012/douthit-for-blatche-alapag-for-castro |archive-date=February 7, 2015 |url-status=live }} McGee and forward [[Keldon Johnson]] of the [[San Antonio Spurs]] were announced as replacements for [[Bradley Beal]] and [[Kevin Love]] on the [[2020 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2020 U.S. Olympic team]].{{Cite web|title=Kevin Love out of Olympics; JaVale McGee, Keldon Johnson joining Team USA, sources say|url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/31827912|publisher=ESPN|date=July 16, 2021 }} On August 7, 2021, McGee won an Olympic gold medal after United States defeated [[France men's national basketball team|France]] in the final. With the medal, he and his mother, [[Pamela McGee]], became the first mother and son to win gold medals in Olympic history.{{cite news |last=Edmunds |first=Ashton |title=Pamela and JaVale McGee become the first mother-son gold-medal duo in Olympics history |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/31977111|access-date=August 7, 2021 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=August 7, 2021}} ==Philanthropy== In 2013, McGee started Juglife Foundation, an organization that brings awareness of drinking water and hydration. He has hosted celebrity [[softball]] games involving his NBA colleagues.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ktvu.com/news/warriors-javale-mcgee-hosts-4th-annual-charity-softball-game-with-teammates-celebrities|title=Warriors' JaVale McGee hosts 4th annual charity softball game with teammates, celebrities|date=June 22, 2018|website=KTVU FOX 2|language=en-US|access-date=November 29, 2019}} Juglife has partnered with Hope 4 Kids International in building wells in [[Uganda]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.slamonline.com/nba/juglife-how-javale-mcgee-is-saving-lives-through-his-foundation/|title=JUGLIFE: How JaVale McGee Is Saving Lives Through His Foundation|date=November 19, 2018|website=SLAM|language=en|access-date=November 29, 2019}} ==Personal life== McGee's father, {{convert|6|ft|10|in|adj=on}} [[George Montgomery (basketball)|George Montgomery]], was a [[1985 NBA draft|1985 second-round draft]] selection by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], though he did not play for the team. His mother, {{convert|6|ft|3|in|adj=on}} [[Pamela McGee]], was a [[University of Southern California]] standout who played with her twin sister, [[Paula McGee|Paula]], and [[Cheryl Miller]], and won two NCAA Division I championships, in 1983 and 1984.[https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1985-04-20-sp-21839-story.html PAM AND PAULA McGEE: DOUBLE FIGURES], ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'', Mike DiGiovanna, April 20, 1985. Retrieved June 25, 2017. Prior to that, Pamela won two Michigan state championships at Northern Flint High School. She won an Olympic gold medal in [[Basketball at the 1984 Summer Olympics|1984]]. Besides playing in France, Italy and Brazil, Pamela was drafted in the [[1997 WNBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Monarchs]], and played for the Monarchs and [[Los Angeles Sparks]]. McGee is the first son of a WNBA player to ever play in the NBA.{{cite web |last=Lundblad |first=Jeremy |date=May 16, 2008 |title=Mother-son legacy a first for WNBA/NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2008/columns/story?page=080513-mcgee |access-date=May 25, 2023 |publisher=ESPN}} His younger half-sister, [[Imani McGee-Stafford]], is also a professional basketball player who previously played in the WNBA for both the [[Chicago Sky]] and the [[Atlanta Dream]].{{cite web|url=http://www.wnba.com/news/imani-boyette-wnba-draft-texas-pam-mcgee/|title=Imani Boyette Follows in Mother's Footsteps, Finds Perfect Fit in Chicago – WNBA.com – Official Site of the WNBA}} His mother, with a degree in economics, balanced her international basketball career with raising both children, homeschooling, coaching and teaching school in the offseason.[https://www.chicagotribune.com/1998/10/11/wnbas-mcgee-daughter-deserve-better/ Wnba's Mcgee, Daughter Deserve Better], ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'', Melissa Isaacson, October 11, 1998. Retrieved June 25, 2017.[https://theringer.com/2017-nba-finals-golden-state-warriors-javale-mcgee-pamela-mcgee-d409a6bb1202 Like Mother, Like Son], ''[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]],'' Katie Baker, June 7, 2017. Retrieved June 25, 2017. McGee is also cousins with former [[NFL]] defensive end [[Jarron Gilbert]].{{cite web|last=Maloney|first=Jack|url=https://www.wnba.com/news/rookie-report-imani-boyette-chicago-sky-50-cent/|title=Rookie Report: Hate It Or Love It, Imani Boyette's On Top|work=wnba.com|date=August 5, 2016|access-date=May 5, 2019|quote=Between her mother, her father (Kevin Stafford, who played overseas) her brother (JaVale McGee, who plays in the NBA), her cousin (Jarron Gilbert, who played in the NFL)...}} In 2013, it was announced that McGee would be starring in his own reality television show, ''[[Mom's Got Game]]'', with his mother.{{cite web|last=Highkin|first=Sean|title=JaVale McGee is starring in a reality show with his mom|url=http://ftw.usatoday.com/2013/12/nba-javale-pam-mcgee-oprah-reality-show/|work=USA Today Sports|accessdate=August 11, 2021|date=December 23, 2013}} McGee had the largest documented [[armspan]] of any current NBA player at {{height|ft=7|in=6.5}}{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrpdA5BRx3U|title=Sport Science: JaVale McGee|last=ESPN Player|date=February 18, 2012|via=YouTube}} until the Nuggets drafted [[Rudy Gobert]], with an armspan at {{height|ft=7|in=8.5}} in the [[2013 NBA draft]]. McGee has been featured regularly on ''[[Inside the NBA]]''{{'}}s basketball blooper feature "[[Shaqtin' a Fool]]", earning the nickname "Tragic Bronson", a play on [[Magic Johnson]], from [[Shaquille O'Neal]].{{cite web|url=http://hangtime.blogs.nba.com/category/shaqtin-a-fool/|title=Shaqtin A Fool " NBA.com – Hang Time Blog|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=March 13, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140528204653/http://hangtime.blogs.nba.com/category/shaqtin-a-fool/|archive-date=May 28, 2014|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f69IDWEyBek|title=Shaqtin' A Fool – The Best of the Worst of JaVale McGee|last=jslv94|date=April 25, 2012|via=YouTube}} McGee has expressed displeasure at his frequent appearance on the segment.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/gameon/2013/03/08/javale-mcgee-shaquille-oneal-tnt-awkward-interview/1972991/|title=Wait, what did JaVale McGee say about Shaquille O'Neal?|website=[[USA Today]] }} McGee became a full-time [[vegan]] in the summer of 2017. He had dabbled with the diet for a few years, using it before each season to lose weight. McGee committed to it full-time after seeing how his body responded during the Warriors' championship season in 2016–17.{{cite web|last=Cason|first=Christopher|url=https://www.gq.com/story/javale-mcgee-real-life-diet|title=The Real-Life Diet of JaVale McGee, Vegan|work=GQ|date=February 27, 2018|access-date=March 4, 2018}} McGee is also a record producer under the moniker Pierre. He has a studio in [[Inglewood, California|Inglewood]] and released his self-titled debut album in 2018.{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2800455-qa-with-javale-mcgee-his-take-on-music-basketball-and-the-king|title=JaVale McGee Releases New Song and Talks About His Music and the New Lakers|last=Sepkowitz|first=Leo|website=Bleacher Report|language=en|access-date=February 23, 2020}} In 2020, McGee co-produced "Available" with [[Poo Bear]] and HARV on [[Justin Bieber]]'s record, [[Changes (Justin Bieber album)|''Changes'']].{{cite web |url=https://music.apple.com/us/song/available/1496639601 |title=Available - Song by Justin Bieber |accessdate=June 25, 2024 |date=February 14,
